central_question: How will quantum computing develop in the United States, China, and the European Union from 2026 through 2040 across hardware modalities, funding, supply chains and security policy, and what will its economic and cryptographic impact be?

situation_brief.current_situation: Quantum computing has passed from the NISQ era into early error correction in the laboratory: Google's Willow (105 qubits, December 2024) demonstrated below-threshold surface-code error correction and claimed the first verifiable quantum advantage in October 2025; Quantinuum's Helios (November 2025) holds the fidelity frontier with 99.921% all-pairs two-qubit fidelity and 48 error-corrected logical qubits; China's Zuchongzhi 3.2 (December 2025) replicated below-threshold correction about a year behind Google. Global revenue was only $1.4 billion in 2025 (QED-C) but private investment surged to $12.6 billion in 2025 and cumulative public commitments reached $56.7 billion.
situation_brief.context: Vendor roadmaps cluster first fault-tolerant machines at 2028-2030 (IBM Starling 2029, QuEra Libra 2028, Quantinuum Apollo ~2030) while calibrated expert judgment (GRI 2025: 28-49% CRQC probability within ten years) and BCG (full fault tolerance after 2040) sit later. NIST draft IR 8547 would deprecate RSA/ECC after 2030 and disallow after 2035; US federal migration is costed at ~$7.1 billion. Export controls (US September 2024 rule, EU September 2025 alignment, Entity List additions) and China's rare-earth retaliation are splitting supply chains.
situation_brief.dynamics: A 2025 funding boom (private investment 6.3x 2024 levels) runs ahead of demonstrated commercial value; DARPA's QBI independently tests utility-scale claims by 2033; helium-3 and dilution refrigerators form a European-controlled choke point that China is localizing around; harvest-now-decrypt-later makes the security window effectively open today, so PQC migration costs land before quantum commercial value.
fault_lines: Vendor fault-tolerance claims versus independent expert timelines and DARPA verification
US private-capital-led leadership versus China's opaque state funding (~$15 billion cited, unverifiable) versus EU coordinated deployment
Export controls accelerating Chinese self-sufficiency while disrupting its talent and hardware access
Helium-3 and dilution-refrigerator supply concentration in three European firms
Cryptographic risk window: enterprise migration needs 12-15+ years while expert CRQC medians point to mid-to-late 2030s
catalysts: IBM Starling delivery at specification (2029) or milestone slips
DARPA QBI Stage C verification verdicts by 2033
Google's next milestone, a long-lived logical qubit requiring millions of components
NIST finalization of IR 8547 and federal migration deadlines
IonQ's ~10,000-qubit Oxford Ionics chip promised for 2027
Annual GRI expert survey revisions of CRQC probability

Zuchongzhi 3.2 (107 qubits) below-threshold error correction published in PRL (distance-7, Λ = 1.40(6)).
Senator Todd Young introduces S.3597, the National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act of 2026.
US House passes the Remote Access Security Act 369-22 to extend export controls to remote cloud access.
MOFCOM announces broad controls on rare-earth and battery materials and technology (announced 9 October 2025 per report; March 2026 QBIT solicitation also this month).
DARPA publishes QBIT Stage A solicitation (DARPA-PA-26-02-02) with 30 November 2026 deadline.
US Senate Commerce Committee orders S.3597 reported favorably with a substitute amendment.
House Science Committee markup where Ranking Member Lofgren states the bill 'does not have any funds authorized'.
IQM announces directional tile codes, targeting fault tolerance by 2030.
Zhejiang University group publishes first demonstration of zero-noise extrapolation on logical qubits in Nature Communications.
EuroHPC had procured and inaugurated six quantum computers across Europe by this date.
US Commerce interim final rule effective (89 FR 72926) adding quantum technologies to the Commerce Control List.
US outbound investment rules effective, prohibiting US investment in Chinese quantum computing, military quantum sensing and quantum communication.
USTC posts programmable 3,050-photon Gaussian boson sampling demonstration (arXiv:2508.09092).
H.R. 6213 reported, would have authorized $1.8 billion for FY2025-2029; lapsed without enactment.
BIS adds seven Chinese supply-chain entities including cryogenics companies Scikro and Physike.
NIST releases initial public draft of IR 8547 transition plan.
Global Risk Institute / evolutionQ Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025 published (26 experts).

scenarios.name: Steady climb
scenarios.narrative: Incremental progress on roadmaps delivers early fault-tolerant machines around 2030-2033 with the US leading, moderate commercial value by 2035 and cryptographic relevance after 2035.

scenarios.name: Quantum leap
scenarios.narrative: Error-correction breakthroughs in one modality (likely superconducting or neutral-atom) deliver utility-scale quantum computing before 2030, triggering large economic value and an urgent PQC crisis.

scenarios.name: Long winter
scenarios.narrative: Scaling stalls on fidelity and overhead across all modalities, commercial value stays niche through 2035, and hype-driven funding retrenches while China's state funding sustains catch-up.

scenarios.name: Fragmented multipolarity
scenarios.narrative: Different regions lead different modalities and applications, export controls split supply chains, and no single region dominates fault tolerance or commercial advantage by 2035.
